errors.text: The hypothesis redirects the target problem from solid–liquid free energies and melting-point prediction to phase decomposition, B2 clustering, and diffuse antiphase-boundary energetics.

It does not clearly reconstruct direct MTP-to-DFT free energy perturbation; instead it ambiguously includes coupling-parameter thermodynamic integration, the expensive step that was supposed to be replaced.

It assigns SRO and ordered clusters as the principal mediator while omitting the target mechanism of low-variance MTP–DFT energy differences in liquid-phase sampling and the electronic Gibbs-energy contribution associated with the density of states near the Fermi level.

The proposed falsification study lacks held-out DFT free-energy or ab initio TI ground truth, so agreement or disagreement among EAM and differently trained MTPs cannot establish that an apparent efficiency gain is physically accurate rather than a shared potential artifact.
